chunks.heading: Details of each Segment
chunks.text:
- During the week (20th Mar 2025 – 26th Mar 2025), lower rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 32%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01th Mar to 26th Mar 2025) is lower than LPA by 24%. Rainfall Forecast: 27th Mar – 02nd April 2025 a) Isolated to scattered light/moderate rainfall accompanied with thunderstorm, lightning & gusty winds (speed 30-50 kmph) likely over Madhya Maharashtra, North Interior Karnataka on 29th & 30th , Konkan & Goa on 29th; Marathawada on 30th; Kerala & Mahe, South Interior Karnataka during 27th -31st; Coastal Karnataka, Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam on 27th, 30th & 31st March. b) No significant weather likely over rest parts of the country during the week. 03rd – 09th April, 2025 a) Under the influence of western disturbances, scattered to fairly widespread rainfall/snowfall is likely over Western Himalayan Region during some days of the week.
| 4 b) Light/moderate isolated to scattered rainfall is likely over northeast India and south Peninsular & adjoining central India during some to many days of the week. c) Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India and below normal over rest parts of the country during the week.

chunks.text:
Temperature Forecast 27th Mar – 02nd April 2025 a) Gradual fall in maximum temperatures by 3-5°C likely over Northwest India during next 3 days and rise by 2-3°C thereafter.
| 5 b) Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over East India during next 2 days and no significant change thereafter. c) No significant change in maximum temperatures over Gujarat state during next 3 days and rise by 2-3°C thereafter. d) Gradual fall in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C likely over Central India during next 3 days and no significant change thereafter. e) Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal or near normal over most parts of the country.

chunks.heading: 4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION
chunks.text:
Soil Moisture Observation - Soil moisture during 22 – 28 March 2025 is better/similar to the average of the past 9 years in A.P, Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Rajasthan, M.P, Punjab, Haryana and Maharashtra. - Whereas it is lower than average of past 9 years avg. in parts of Bihar, Northern W.B., Chhattisgarh, Eastern U.P & in a parts of southern & western Odisha. - These is improvement is soil moisture in Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha state due to rainfall activity during last week. (b) Temperature Observation
| 7


Preliminary area coverage of Summer Crops - As on 28.03.2025, about 75.6 percent of the normal area has been sown under the summer crops - Rice: About 30.50 lakh ha area coverage under Summer Rice has been reported as compared to 26.55 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Pulses: About 8.40 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 7.50 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. - Oilseeds: About 6.04 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 6.32 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
